factory.title: Claude Software Factory
factory.summary: A set of skills, rules, deterministic gates and eight Sonnet-pinned agent roles that turn an AI coding assistant from a 'vibe-coder' into a disciplined engineer: requirements are verified before use, tests come before code, the implementer is blind to the tests, QA supervises and verification is deterministic and independent.
detail: The factory is layered. The method (the /sf build loop, its skills and the sf toolchain) runs today. A deterministic engine (the sf CLI) enforces test integrity, one-way-door detection and, through factory/verify, honest solver verdicts on a small pure subset. An agent layer (eight roles, eight hook ids, generator, settings emitter, ledger, walking skeleton) is implemented and acceptance-tested. A lite factory (lsf) runs the same flow in one hour on a laptop with a phase clock, human checkpoints and an offline dashboard.
Click any stacked box to open the diagram inside it. The Coverage tab lists what is built, partial, only designed, outside the repo, or a gap, with reasons.

design.choice: Guard one-way doors; leave two-way doors fast
design.why: Local, reversible work (UI, helpers, cache TTLs) runs autonomously; schemas, auth, public API and vector dimensions need a Socratic debate and an ADR.
design.alternatives: One uniform, rigid process for every change

design.choice: Verification is deterministic; models advise, they do not vote
design.why: Hash baselines, AST scans and hooks cannot be talked around, which is the answer to reward hacking.
design.alternatives: LLM committees grading each other's work

coverage.note: The method, the sf CLI and tool groups, the eight-role agent layer (generator, settings emitter, eight hook ids, ledger, stage graph, walking skeleton), slices, intake, structure, contracts/solver, the QA loop, the ops dashboard and the lite factory (lsf) are implemented and tested. Test and eval counts are recorded in docs/sf-flow.md ('Evidence base') and docs/adr/ADR-0005-sonnet-only-roles-and-qa-role.md section 3; this explorer cites them instead of restating them. Real headless sessions verified the hooks, the qa role and the self-updating dashboard (docs/native-verification/2026-10-19/REPORT.md, docs/native-verification/2026-10-20/REPORT.md); the intake gate, a full QA loop with real agents, reviewer amendments and interactive use have not run in a real session.

The Bash and blindness guards are command-text guards and cannot be complete; the OS sandbox is the backstop (see the residual-risk sections of docs/hooks/bash_guard.md and blindness_guard.md)
One acceptance case is open by design pending a decision: TB06-D-035 (docs/adr/ADR-0004)

intake.title: Requirements intake and sweep
intake.summary: Before any line of a brief becomes a requirement, it is transcribed verbatim, swept for traps (licences, provider terms, impossible guarantees, inverted rubrics), settled by research and experiments, and only then written into a PRD and a requirements ledger.
detail: Every line of prose in a source brief is a requirement, including 'optional' items and out-of-scope lists. The ledger is the one summary table allowed to exist because stage 9 of the loop rebuilds its touched rows from the source every time.

design.choice: Sweep the brief before trusting it
design.why: Briefs and rubrics can carry traps: a licence you cannot meet, a guarantee theory rules out, a rubric that rewards the wrong thing. Finding them after building is far more expensive.
design.alternatives: Trusting the PRD as written

design.choice: The sweep is a loop, not a one-shot gate
design.why: Suspects are settled with grounded research and experiments until the loop converges; the PRD is written only after.
design.alternatives: A single checklist pass

build-loop.title: Build loop (/sf)
build-loop.summary: The fixed twelve-stage loop every implementation slice follows, bound into a checklist with one todo per stage so a skipped stage is visible instead of forgotten.
detail: The loop is not a variable: schedule pressure may reorder or slice work smaller but never drop a stage. The run ends when every requirement line is satisfied or recorded as blocked with what it waits on, not when a queue empties.

design.choice: Make the back half of the loop a checklist
design.why: Research and experiments are interesting and get done; tests-first, blind implementation, separate runner, adversarial review and drift check cost time without visible progress, so they quietly vanish. A todo per stage makes a skip visible.
design.alternatives: A process document consulted from memory

coverage.note: Fully written and in daily use on other projects; absent for this repository itself.
gaps: The installed skill is the only copy: the repository's own history does not version it

adrs.title: Architecture decision records
adrs.summary: ADR-0001 chooses the Unity-IR dual-plane substrate, ADR-0002 the zero-trust verification substrate, ADR-0003 agent roles above skills, ADR-0004 (proposed) the blindness guard and symlinks, ADR-0005 Sonnet for every role plus a qa role and the test and eval edits that followed.

design.choice: Unity-IR (ADR-0001)
design.why: A deterministic three-layer schema decouples reasoning from lexical syntax; reviewers audit semantic delta rather than lines.
design.alternatives: Raw polyglot source in the model context

design.choice: Zero-trust verification (ADR-0002)
design.why: Hashed baselines, design-by-contract and symbolic exploration remove reward hacking structurally.
design.alternatives: Trusting model-written tests

design.choice: Roles above skills (ADR-0003)
design.why: Split by context boundary, not pipeline phase; one writer per tree; hooks enforce, prompts advise.
design.alternatives: A fixed seven-stage relay

design.choice: Sonnet for every role, plus a qa role (ADR-0005)
design.why: The owner's flow asks for one model across roles and QA agents that supervise and re-initiate; the loader, installer and doctor reject any other model unless explicitly allowed.
design.alternatives: Per-role model tiers (Opus to author, Haiku to run) proposed in the 2026-09-24 design

flow-lb-qa-impl.summary: A failed gate gives behavioural feedback (criterion terms, no test source, leak-checked) and the same tier retries; at the policy point the model tier escalates; at the cap the case is handed to the reviewer. The role graph declares the loop [qa, implement].

flow-lb-qa-evals.title: Loop 2: QA to evals
flow-lb-qa-evals.summary: When the same failure signature recurs, QA proposes a regression case (sf qa regression-propose, written append-only to regression-proposals/<signature>.md) which goes back to the evals stage; the evals stay frozen except through an additive amendment.
